WORTH AN AFTERNOON, and the afternoon is real now: the schema blocker is gone, doc/builder.md:376 has the right four steps, and I checked the one cost the doc calls free - Build wearing the realm's bar needs one line (stage.changed = (axis, value) => this.set_words({[axis]: value})), because PagingStage.set() already calls changed(). assign.outcome:
**Eight of my nine landed, the url seam is genuinely finished — and the exit test is not passed, because the pages the realm MAKES are broken in two ways I had not looked at before.**

**The seam is done.** Every configuration has an address and the address works cold, in-app, and both ways. I measured it end to end: `/imagine/paging/room/wide/?navigation=columns&surface=dark` opens right; changing one of the bar's seven dropdowns writes `?navigation=columns`; a `cross/` cell click lands on the hub wearing the two words it was crossing; and `?nest=` round-trips — one chip of twelve lit on [the nest preset](/imagine/paging/library/nest/), clicking it off removes the nested page, picking another writes `?nest=magazine`, and a cold reload of a `?nest=` url comes back nested. Zero page errors across 52 loads at 1280 and 3440, and the stylesheets have **no dead rules left** — I resolved every apparent orphan to the code that composes it.

**One vocabulary, and it holds.** `blocks.js` is the only place the seven words exist; both editors re-export it; there is no hand-typed copy anywhere. That was the big one and it is done.

![A page you made, at 1280 — its tab strip reads Overview, Pricing, Docs, Contact, and its real children are Today and Later](shots/made-notes-1280.png)

**But look at the picture.** That is `/imagine/paging/make/notes/` — a page **you** made, whose navigation word is `tabs`, which really has two children called **Today** and **Later**. It draws four tabs called *Overview, Pricing, Docs, Contact* — the demo's canned samples — and carries **zero links to its own children**. `make/page.js` puts a stage on the page and never tells it what the page's children are.

**And the blocks you add in Build are drawn by nothing.** Build's fifth control collects prose blocks, card walls and templates; they are saved to disk inside `mode`; and outside `build/` nothing in the realm reads them. Open the page you built and you get the generic content sample instead. It is the same defect the last pass fixed for the seven words — a control writing a key nothing reads — moved one level down.

**The builder is one column at 1280.** Its card is 957px, under its own 64rem floor, so the three tracks stack and the live stage lands **2,100px down** — two folds below the first screen, on the page whose whole claim is "the middle column is the page assembling as you click". At 1920 and 3440 it is fine (537px and 632px down).

**`BuildStage` → `PagingStage`, ruled.** Worth an afternoon, and the afternoon is real now — the schema blocker is gone, [doc/builder.md](/imagine/paging/doc/builder/) has the right four steps, and the one cost it calls free really is one line. It deletes 232 lines of `build/stage.js` and 43 of `build/build.css` and gives Build four words it cannot set today. **But it is not the next afternoon.** What a newcomer notices is not the tool's picture, it is the page they keep — and deciding what happens to Build's blocks is what decides the merge's shape, so the two belong in one afternoon rather than two. Order: fix the children, decide the blocks, then merge.

**Still seven stage renderers**, and the one waiting to be merged **grew** from 208 to 232 lines — the last pass copied the stage's bar, panel and aside into it, and the two copies already disagree (four properties rows against three).
